sentences.text: Branta rhuax, known as the giant Hawaii goose, was an extinct species of goose found only on the island of Hawaii.
This bird belongs to the family Anatidae, which includes modern ducks, geese, and swans.
It holds the distinction of being the first fossil bird ever described from the Hawaiian Islands.
The specific epithet 'rhuax' is derived from the Greek word for lava stream.
The fossil bones were found near Kaumaikeohu, above Pahala in the Kau District of the Island of Hawaii, beneath a prehistoric lava flow and on top of an ash bed.
The fossil bones were friable and warped because they were subjected to intense heat from the lava.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a fragmentary right tibiotarsus held by the United States National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C.
The species lived during the Holocene epoch, from 0.0117 million years ago to the present.
Olson and James (1991) considered the available material too imperfect to determine the bird's affinities precisely, suggesting its relationships remained doubtful until more specimens were found.
